<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**14** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **177** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cac93cc627357bef93b0654b912bb75579415fc7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7440791295a1b8ca9438b651fb9e9944bc8b4ab8` — the merge of head `c840b723e400ca3e9dadebb714528f3d8cb3652f` into base `cac93cc627357bef93b0654b912bb75579415fc7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7440791295a1b8ca9438b651fb9e9944bc8b4ab8 && git checkout 7440791295a1b8ca9438b651fb9e9944bc8b4ab8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin cac93cc627357bef93b0654b912bb75579415fc7 c840b723e400ca3e9dadebb714528f3d8cb3652f && git checkout -B drift-repro cac93cc627357bef93b0654b912bb75579415fc7 && git merge --no-ff c840b723e400ca3e9dadebb714528f3d8cb3652f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json cac93cc627357bef93b0654b912bb75579415fc7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `04eb2c057302c59f93e2b343a558241b6255e856`
Local-runs: probe — read-only static AST scans of `packages/spec/src` on `main` (nothing built, tested or re-run): neither the diff nor the check-runs can name which module-scope initializers the wrapper touches or what they call
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/spec/tsup.config.ts, packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts

First round. Inputs: card #37572 (body, 2 comments), #37444 (body, 6 comments, ruling 7205984444), the PR body, its 9 files and the net diff at this head, the check-runs on this head, and the cited code read on `main` at `3ed97b71`. The rest of the diff (`ui/**`, the changeset's prose) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Gates: read at 2026-11-27T03:58Z, about 15 minutes into CI on this head. 30 check-runs green, none red: `Build Core`, both `Check Changeset` runs, `Lint & Repo Gates` and the Lint families, `Lint UI`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Type Check · consumer gates`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Live E2E UI`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Test Core (9/10)` and one `Test UI` shard. **27 still running**: `Test Core` (9 of 10 shards), `Test UI` (15 of 16), `Build & E2E UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Type Check · workspace`. 12 skipped; the one cancelled `PR-body guards` run was replaced by a green one. The running ones are not judged here, and two of them carry claims this record leans on: the workspace type check holds the `satisfies` clause, and a `Test Core` shard runs the ledger test. Read them before this record is used.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@objectstack/spec` public surface: unchanged. Right.** No export is added, removed or retyped. `TRANSLATED_METADATA_TYPE_NAMES` and the `MetadataDocumentTranslator` type are module-private.
- **`@objectstack/spec` accept set: unchanged. Right.** No schema is edited; `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.
- **`TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES`: same set, same order. Right.** The table on `main` has 13 keys (`view`, `action`, `object`, `app`, `dashboard`, `dataset`, `page`, `picklist`, `position`, `permission`, `report`, `book`, `mapping`) and the new list spells the same 13 in the same order. The declared type is still a read-only set of strings. Every reader on `main` asks `.has()` or spreads it into another set (`packages/rest/src/meta-item-read-gate.ts:3294`, the runtime parity test), so none depends on order.
- **`@objectstack/spec` published JS: shape changes, values do not. Right as described.** A replica of the PR's own decision functions over `main` wraps 2,037 of 5,185 initialised module-scope declarations and leaves 13 alone, the same 13 `Object.assign(ExistingSchema, { create })` sites the PR lists. A process that loads the dist unbundled (server, CLI, plugins) still evaluates every initializer: spec's own build can only drop a binding nothing reads, and `main` has no unexported module-scope variable that nothing else in its file names (0 found).
- **`.d.ts`: untouched by the transform. Right.** The pass is an esbuild `onLoad` plugin. It runs for the ESM and CJS outputs, the `browser/` outputs and the node-side copies (both `onLoad` sites are changed). The declaration pass (`BUILD_DTS=true`, `dts.only`) reads the original sources and never calls it. The only declaration bytes that move are the edited jsdoc on `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES`.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-form`: its published `./core` entry gains one export, `createKeepsField`. A widening, declared as none. Wrong: see S2.**
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/console`, `@objectstack/console`: no surface change. Right.** One import specifier and one chunk rule.

### ② Semver level

The declared line, `Clause-②: no`, is wrong for the change as a whole: it should read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. `no` is right for `@objectstack/spec` (its published JS changes shape; no accept set and no export moves), but the line answers for every package in the changeset, and `@object-ui/plugin-form/core` gains a member.

`patch` on all five packages is right: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch` too (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3). `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

**S2 (should-fix) — the `Clause-②` line is wrong for `@object-ui/plugin-form`.** `ui/packages/plugin-form/src/core.ts` adds `export { createKeepsField }` to the published `@object-ui/plugin-form/core` subpath. The repo's own precedent calls exactly this a widening: changeset `9e6533b` ("one new export, `relatedCreateSeedOf`, on the published `@object-ui/plugin-detail/core` subpath; nothing is removed or renamed, and the package root exports the same names as before") and the changeset that first put `createKeepsField` on the package root (`ui/packages/plugin-form/CHANGELOG.md:268`). Fix: `Clause-②: yes (widening)` with the one export named, in the PR body and in the changeset. The level stays `patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`Part of #37444`, `Part of #37572`: right on both.** #37572 expects the first load to stop pulling the spec schemas the first screen does not need; `vendor-objectstack` is still 647,764 bytes gzipped and the PR names six schemas that keep it there. #37444 closes at a median of at most 2500 ms on all three pages over HTTPS with HTTP/2; the PR reads list 2652 and record 2640.5. Neither card is delivered whole.
- **#37572's third expectation is still owed**: the new medians are in the PR body, not yet on #37444. The seat records them there when this lands.
- **The readings are medians of 10 (two rounds of 5, reversed), HTTP/2 only.** That is a wider sample than the ruling's median of 5, and ruling 7205984444 makes HTTP/1.1 a control only. No acceptance is claimed, so nothing is owed here; the closing reading on #37444 is still to be taken as the ruling words it.
- **"Narrower spec exports are a separate change"**: agreed. Exporting sub-schemas is a spec surface widening and needs its own card. None is cited; escalated to the seat to file or name it, since #37572 stays open on exactly that.
- **`BASELINE` names the branch commit `003fde60` with `squashMerge: null`**: the back-fill after merge is the lane seat's file and duty.
- **`open_questions`**: none stated in the PR or on the card.
- **SQL push-down**: nothing to judge. The diff has no query, no id list and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. Two should-fix (S1 here, S2 under ②), both owing a delta review.

**`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` — holds.** Against the code it cites: the table and the list agree today (above). The `satisfies` clause sits on the object literal, so it checks both directions: a missing name is a missing property, and an extra translator is an excess property. The wider annotation on the table keeps the `[type]` lookup in `translateMetadataDocument` as it was. Against its scenario: a reader of the set now reaches the name list only; the list is a literal, the table is a literal of names, and the set's own initializer is wrapped. Tried to break it: order (the type check does not hold order, and no reader needs it), duplicates (a set), a reader that iterates (none).

**`packages/spec/tsup.config.ts` — the transform holds; its safety account does not.**

- Semantics, order and TDZ hold. The arrow is called in place with no arguments, so a kept initializer runs at the same point as before, and closures see the same bindings. A bundler keeps what a kept initializer reads, because the read is a reference. `main` has no module-scope class expression (whose inferred name would be lost) and no `await`, `this` or destructuring pattern in a wrapped declaration. Arrows and function expressions are left unwrapped, so their names survive.
- Sites that write outside themselves, each read on `main`:
  - `Object.assign(ExistingSchema, { create })`, 13 sites: skipped by the wrapper. Right.
  - `componentSlot(...)` (5 sites) and `declare(...)`, called directly or through `requiredOneOf`: a `WeakMap` keyed by the schema or predicate the same initializer just built. Wrapped, safe, in the ledger.
  - zod's `.describe()` and `.meta()`: registered against the clone they return; no `meta` id is used outside a test. Wrapped, safe.
  - **`withRefusalHead(prescription, head)`, 6 sites, `data/query.zod.ts:104, 111, 241, 429, 448, 462`: wrapped, and it registers into a process-wide map on `globalThis` (`shared/refusal-head.ts:59-90`). Not in the ledger; the scan cannot see it.**
  - **`strictObjectError` pushes every strict object's declaration into a process-wide store (`shared/strict-object.ts:242, 383`). Not in the ledger either.** Its only readers are spec's own tests and `scripts/build-schemas.ts`, which run from source, and `strictObject` has been marked since #10031.
- Nothing breaks today. Each of the six prescriptions is raised only through the constant that registers it (`query.zod.ts:183-184, 322, 617-635`, `data-engine.zod.ts:157, 207`, `api/protocol.zod.ts:3403`, `objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts:654-655`), so any bundle that can raise the text keeps the registration.

**`packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts` — a real guard, narrower than its account.** The wrapper cases pin the transform on synthetic text, the fixture consumer has its control (the reader keeps the schema the helper-only consumer drops), and the ledger case has a floor and an exact comparison. What the ledger case does not do is in S1.

**S1 (should-fix) — the docblock and the ledger test claim a guard that is not there.** `wrapModuleScopeInitializers`' docblock says that no call at module scope registers into a table, and that the test "reads every module-scope initializer of this package's sources and refuses one that calls a function writing to a module-level binding". Neither sentence agrees with the tree:
  1. Six module-scope initializers do register (`withRefusalHead`), and every `strictObject` does too. The safety argument for them (the registering constant is the one every raiser reads; the store is read only from source) is true but written nowhere.
  2. The test never reads a module-scope initializer. It lists the module-level bindings that some function writes and compares that list to the ledger. A new module-scope call of a writer already in the ledger (`registerMetadataTypeSchema(...)` at module scope, say) changes nothing in that list and stays green.
  3. The scan sees a write only when its receiver is rooted in a module-level name. It misses a receiver that is a call (`registry().set(...)`, `declarationStore().push(...)`: the two real sites), `globalThis`, a receiver under an `as` cast, and a helper that writes to its own parameter.
  
  The test is not vacuous: its floor and its exact comparison would red on a new cache. But it guards less than the docblock and the PR body say it does. Fix: make the account and the instrument agree. Name the two families with the reason each may be dropped, and either teach the test what the docblock says (a module-scope initializer calling a writer is refused unless listed) or cut the docblock down to what the test holds.

Nits, no effect on correctness or the contract; none is worth moving a file for on its own:

- N1 (nit): `i18n-resolver.ts` still says in unchanged comments that the set "is derived below" and that registering in the table "is the whole wiring" (the `dataset` comment inside the table at `:2045`; the dataset translator's docblock at `:2748`). A new type now takes its name in the list too. The type check asks for it, so nobody can ship the gap.
- N2 (nit): `writesToAnExistingObject` stops at every function boundary, so it would not see a callback that runs at load (a `LIST.map(...)` callback that calls `Object.assign(Existing, ...)`, a source-level IIFE), and `isFreshValue` takes any call result as fresh. `main` has no such site: 3 source-level IIFE initializers, none writing module state, and the 3 wrapped `Object.assign` calls all take a new arrow first.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c840b723e400ca3e9dadebb714528f3d8cb3652f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts + packages/spec/tsup.config.ts, packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts

DELTA review from `04eb2c057302c59f93e2b343a558241b6255e856` (record 7209422545: PASS, should-fix S1 and S2, nits N1 and N2) to this head. One commit, `c840b723`, four files: the changeset, the test, `i18n-resolver.ts` and `tsup.config.ts`. Inputs: that delta, the PR body at this head, comment 7209516099 on #37444, the check-runs on both heads, and the cited code on `main`.

Gates: read at 2026-11-27T04:11Z, about 4 minutes into CI on this head. 12 check-runs green, none red: both `Check Changeset` runs, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check PR Size`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, the docs flag, both shard planners, `Auto Label`, `filter`. **25 still running**: all ten `Test Core` shards, `Build Core`, `Build UI Deps`, the eight Lint families, the four Type Check families and `Live E2E UI`; no `Test UI` shard has started. 12 skipped; one cancelled `PR-body guards` run was replaced by a green one. On the previous head CI finished with 57 green and none red, `Type Check · workspace` among them; three `Test Core` shards (3, 5, 6 of 10) were cancelled by this push and never answered. So the ledger test, with its two new cases, has **no CI answer on this head yet**. Read `Test Core` and `Type Check · workspace` here before this record is used.

### ① Derived judgments

- **No accept set and no public surface moves in the delta. Right.** Both hunks in the one published source, `i18n-resolver.ts`, are inside comments: four line comments in the translator table and one docblock. The `tsup.config.ts` hunk is inside the `wrapModuleScopeInitializers` docblock, so the transform does what it did at the previous head. The test file is not published.
- **Published bytes: comments, and what follows from them. Right as the dev describes it.** No executable token changes. The docblock on the dataset translator is emitted into the declarations, three lines are added above the rest of `i18n-resolver.ts` so its source map shifts, and chunk names follow chunk content. Judged from the diff; nothing was built here.
- **The round-1 judgments on `TRANSLATABLE_METADATA_TYPES`, the transform and the `.d.ts` pass stand.** The delta touches none of that code.

### ② Semver level

- **S2: closed.** The changeset and the PR body now read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and name the one export, `createKeepsField` on the published `@object-ui/plugin-form/core` subpath, in the words of the `9e6533b` precedent. Both say `@objectstack/spec`'s surface does not change. `patch` on all five packages stands, and `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **#37572's third expectation: answered.** The medians are on #37444 (7209516099), named as HTTP/2 readings of a build not yet merged.
- **The narrower-exports follow-up still has no card number.** The #37444 comment calls it "a separate card". The seat files or names it.
- **N2 and the nits below are left by choice.** A follow-up for them needs a card to be a follow-up; without one they are accepted deviations.
- **SQL push-down**: nothing to judge. The delta has no query, no id list and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix. No should-fix.

- **S1: closed.** All three parts are in the tree.
  1. The scan now reads a write through a type-only cast, through `globalThis`, and through the result of a module-level function declaration. The ledger gains `shared/refusal-head.ts registry()` and `shared/strict-object.ts declarationStore()`, 39 entries. Those are the only two call-result receivers of a writing method in spec's sources on `main`.
  2. A new case reads the calls each module-scope initializer makes outside the functions it defines, follows them by name to the five stores marked as registrations, and refuses a caller the store does not list: `withRefusalHead` only for the refusal heads, any caller for the declaration store, none for the three `registerMetadataType*` stores. It cannot pass empty: it wants more than 1,000 load-time calls and must see both known families reach their store.
  3. The docblock names the two families with the reason each may be dropped, says what the test reads, and says it is a guard on known shapes, not a proof.
- **No module-scope call reaches a registration unlisted today.** Every reference to `withRefusalHead` and to the three `registerMetadataType*` functions in spec's sources is a definition, a string, or one of the six direct calls in `data/query.zod.ts`. There is no import alias, no local alias, no callback and no method that reaches them, so the by-name walk misses nothing that exists.
- **N1: closed.** The table's four comments and the dataset translator's docblock now say the name list is part of the wiring and that the type check asks for both.
- **`packages/spec/src/system/i18n-resolver.ts` — holds**, comments only.
- **`packages/spec/tsup.config.ts` — holds.** The docblock agrees with the test on every claim about today's tree. Two sentences are looser than the code (N3, N4).
- **`packages/spec/scripts/pure-schema-construction.test.ts` — a real guard.** One step is unpinned (N5).

Nits, no effect on correctness or the contract; none moves a file on its own:

- N2 (nit, carried): unchanged, as the dev says.
- N3 (nit): the walk has limits the docblock does not list. A call inside a callback or an IIFE that the initializer runs at load is not read; the fixture pins exactly that (its `[1].map(...)` callback does call `register` at load, and the case asserts the call is not counted). Calls made from object-literal methods, class methods and constructors are not attributed to any name, an aliased import or local alias is a different name, and a store handed out by an arrow constant is not seen (only function declarations are). None of these shapes reaches a restricted store today.
- N4 (nit): "Only code that raises that same constant reads the map" is not literally so. The reader is `refusalHeadOf`, called by the data doors; the raiser is the schema. What holds is that a lookup can only answer for a message raised from the constant, and the raiser reads the constant. The conclusion drawn from it is right.
- N5 (nit): the positive control pins what the verdict is computed from (the store found, the reach through a helper, the load-time call) and stops there. The refusal itself runs only on the real sources, where it must find nothing, so the red path rests on the dev's hand ablation.

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head c840b723e4 · card #37572 (Part of #37444) · area s2-ux · 2026-11-27T04:35Z

**L1 checklist**
- **Shape and checks.** `l1-face.mjs --pr 37786` flags one item, `all-checks`. The flagged run is a `PR-body guards` run (140305545886) that was cancelled when the body was edited mid-run. The later run of the same name, 140305744917, is a success on this head.
